claim: The inflammatory environment of demyelinated lesions in multiple sclerosis (MS) patients contributes to remyelination failure.
source: The inflammatory environment of demyelinated lesions in multiple sclerosis (MS) patients contributes to remyelination failure.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that represents established knowledge in the MS field.

claim: Inflammation activates a cytoprotective pathway, the integrated stress response (ISR).
source: Inflammation activates a cytoprotective pathway, the integrated stress response (ISR), but it remains unclear whether enhancing the ISR can improve remyelination in an inflammatory environment.
evidence: This statement is supported by established scientific knowledge about the ISR pathway.

claim: Genetic ISR enhancement significantly increased the number of remyelinating oligodendrocytes in inflammatory lesions.
source: We demonstrate that either genetic or pharmacological ISR enhancement significantly increased the number of remyelinating oligodendrocytes and remyelinated axons in the inflammatory lesions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, specifically in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Pharmacological ISR enhancement significantly increased the number of remyelinating oligodendrocytes in inflammatory lesions.
source: We demonstrate that either genetic or pharmacological ISR enhancement significantly increased the number of remyelinating oligodendrocytes and remyelinated axons in the inflammatory lesions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, specifically in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Genetic ISR enhancement significantly increased the number of remyelinated axons in inflammatory lesions.
source: We demonstrate that either genetic or pharmacological ISR enhancement significantly increased the number of remyelinating oligodendrocytes and remyelinated axons in the inflammatory lesions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, specifically in Figure 4.

claim: Pharmacological ISR enhancement significantly increased the number of remyelinated axons in inflammatory lesions.
source: We demonstrate that either genetic or pharmacological ISR enhancement significantly increased the number of remyelinating oligodendrocytes and remyelinated axons in the inflammatory lesions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, specifically in Figure 6.

claim: Combined treatment of Sephin1 with bazedoxifene increased myelin thickness of remyelinated axons to pre-lesion levels.
source: Moreover, the combined treatment of the ISR modulator Sephin1 with the oligodendrocyte differentiation enhancing reagent bazedoxifene increased myelin thickness of remyelinated axons to pre-lesion levels.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 8E showing g-ratio measurements.

claim: Prolonging the ISR protects remyelinating oligodendrocytes in the presence of inflammation.
source: Taken together, our findings indicate that prolonging the ISR protects remyelinating oligodendrocytes and promotes remyelination in the presence of inflammation, suggesting that ISR enhancement may provide reparative benefit to MS patients.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from multiple figures (3-8) showing increased oligodendrocyte survival and remyelination.

claim: Prolonging the ISR promotes remyelination in the presence of inflammation.
source: Taken together, our findings indicate that prolonging the ISR protects remyelinating oligodendrocytes and promotes remyelination in the presence of inflammation, suggesting that ISR enhancement may provide reparative benefit to MS patients.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from multiple figures showing increased remyelination metrics.

claim: ISR enhancement may provide reparative benefit to MS patients.

claim: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune inflammatory disorder characterized by focal demyelinated lesions in the CNS.
source: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune inflammatory disorder characterized by focal demyelinated lesions in the CNS (Frohman et al., 2006; Yadav et al., 2015; Reich et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Current immunomodulatory therapies can reduce the frequency and severity of relapses in MS.
source: Although current immunomodulatory therapies can reduce the frequency and severity of relapses, they have demonstrated limited impact on the progression of disease (Dargahi et al., 2017; Hauser and Cree, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Current immunomodulatory therapies have demonstrated limited impact on the progression of MS disease.
source: Although current immunomodulatory therapies can reduce the frequency and severity of relapses, they have demonstrated limited impact on the progression of disease (Dargahi et al., 2017; Hauser and Cree, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Remyelination is the process of restoring demyelinated nerve fibers with new myelin.
source: Remyelination is the process of restoring demyelinated nerve fibers with new myelin, which involves the generation of new mature oligodendrocytes from oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) (Franklin and Ffrench-Constant, 2008a).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Remyelination involves the generation of new mature oligodendrocytes from oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs).
source: Remyelination is the process of restoring demyelinated nerve fibers with new myelin, which involves the generation of new mature oligodendrocytes from oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) (Franklin and Ffrench-Constant, 2008a).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Failure of myelin repair during relapsing-remitting MS leads to chronically demyelinated axons.
source: Failure of myelin repair during relapsing-remitting MS leads to chronically demyelinated axons, which is thought to contribute to axonal degeneration and disease progression (Franklin and Kotter, 2008b; Fancy et al., 2010; Chari, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Chronically demyelinated axons contribute to axonal degeneration and disease progression in MS.
source: Failure of myelin repair during relapsing-remitting MS leads to chronically demyelinated axons, which is thought to contribute to axonal degeneration and disease progression (Franklin and Kotter, 2008b; Fancy et al., 2010; Chari, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The inflammatory environment in MS lesions is considered a major contributor to impaired remyelination.
source: The inflammatory environment in MS lesions is considered a major contributor to impaired remyelination (Starost et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Most remyelination-promoting molecules were identified in in vitro screens under ideal conditions and tested in animal models of non-inflammatory demyelination.
source: A number of small molecules have recently been described to promote OPC maturation and/or enhance remyelination, but most of these molecules were identified in in vitro screens under ideal conditions and tested in animal models of non-inflammatory demyelination (Deshmukh et al., 2013; Mei et al., 2014; Rankin et al., 2019; Najm et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The integrated stress response (ISR) plays a key role in the response of oligodendrocytes to CNS inflammation.
source: The integrated stress response (ISR) plays a key role in the response of oligodendrocytes to CNS inflammation (Chen et al., 2019; Lin et al., 2005; Way et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The ISR is a cytoprotective pathway that is activated by various cytotoxic insults, including inflammation.
source: The ISR is a cytoprotective pathway that is activated by various cytotoxic insults, including inflammation (Costa-Mattioli and Walter, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: The ISR is initiated by phosphorylation of eukaryotic translation initiation factor two alpha (p-eIF2α).
source: The ISR is initiated by phosphorylation of eukaryotic translation initiation factor two alpha (p-eIF2α), by one of four known stress-sensing kinases, to diminish global protein translation and selectively allow for the synthesis of protective proteins.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the ISR pathway mechanism.

claim: p-eIF2α phosphorylation diminishes global protein translation and selectively allows for the synthesis of protective proteins.
source: The ISR is initiated by phosphorylation of eukaryotic translation initiation factor two alpha (p-eIF2α), by one of four known stress-sensing kinases, to diminish global protein translation and selectively allow for the synthesis of protective proteins.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the ISR pathway mechanism.

claim: p-eIF2α is dephosphorylated by the protein phosphatase 1 (PP1)- DNA-damage inducible 34 (GADD34) complex to terminate the ISR upon stress relief.
source: p-eIF2α is dephosphorylated by the protein phosphatase 1 (PP1)- DNA-damage inducible 34 (GADD34) complex to terminate the ISR upon stress relief (Zhang and Kaufman, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Sephin1 disrupts PP1-GADD34 phosphatase activity and prolongs elevated p-eIF2α levels.
source: Sephin1, a recently-identified small molecule, disrupts PP1-GADD34 phosphatase activity and prolongs elevated p-eIF2α levels, thereby enhancing the ISR protective response (Das et al., 2015; Carrara et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Sephin1 enhances the ISR protective response.
source: Sephin1, a recently-identified small molecule, disrupts PP1-GADD34 phosphatase activity and prolongs elevated p-eIF2α levels, thereby enhancing the ISR protective response (Das et al., 2015; Carrara et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: GADD34 deficiency protects mature oligodendrocytes in EAE.
source: We previously showed that GADD34 deficiency or Sephin1 treatment protects matures oligodendrocytes, diminishes demyelination, and delays clinical symptoms in a mouse model of MS, experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) (Chen et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Sephin1 treatment protects mature oligodendrocytes in EAE.
source: We previously showed that GADD34 deficiency or Sephin1 treatment protects matures oligodendrocytes, diminishes demyelination, and delays clinical symptoms in a mouse model of MS, experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) (Chen et al., 2019).

claim: IFN-γ is a pleiotropic T-cell-specific cytokine that stimulates key inflammatory aspects of MS.
source: IFN-γ is a pleotropic T-cell-specific cytokine that stimulates key inflammatory aspects of MS (Lin et al., 2007; Lees and Cross, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: BZA has been shown to enhance OPC differentiation and CNS remyelination in response to focal demyelination.
source: BZA has been shown to enhance OPC differentiation and CNS remyelination in response to focal demyelination (Rankin et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: BZA increases the number of remyelinating oligodendrocytes in the presence of inflammation.
source: We demonstrate that BZA increases the number of remyelinating oligodendrocytes and enhances remyelination in the presence of inflammation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 8.

claim: BZA enhances remyelination in the presence of inflammation.

claim: When combined with Sephin1, BZA further facilitates the remyelinating process.
source: When combined with Sephin1, BZA further facilitates the remyelinating process.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 8.

claim: Sephin1 treatment diminished EAE disease severity in the final week of treatment.
source: Sephin1 (8 mg/kg) or vehicle treatment was initiated in each EAE mouse on the day it reached the peak of disease (clinical score = 3) and was continued to the late stage of EAE, which resulted in diminished EAE disease severity in the final week of Sephin1 treatment (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The presence of axons with thinner myelin sheaths and a higher g-ratio is considered the hallmark of remyelination.
source: The presence of axons with thinner myelin sheaths and a higher g-ratio is considered the hallmark of remyelination (Duncan et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Axons in the spinal cord with a g-ratio greater than 0.8 are likely remyelinated axons in the EAE model.
source: A recent study indicated that axons in the spinal cord with a g-ratio greater than 0.8 are likely remyelinated axons in the EAE model (Mei et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: The density of remyelinated axons (g > 0.8) was significantly higher in EAE mice treated with Sephin1 than those treated with vehicle (p<0.05, η2 = 0.81).
source: Our data demonstrated that the density of remyelinated axons (g > 0.8) was significantly higher in EAE mice treated with Sephin1 than those treated with vehicle (p<0.05, η2 = 0.81) (Figure 1B,C), although no difference was detected in the total number of myelinated axons (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B,C with statistical analysis.

claim: No difference was detected in the total number of myelinated axons between Sephin1 and vehicle treated EAE mice.
source: Our data demonstrated that the density of remyelinated axons (g > 0.8) was significantly higher in EAE mice treated with Sephin1 than those treated with vehicle (p<0.05, η2 = 0.81) (Figure 1B,C), although no difference was detected in the total number of myelinated axons (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Sephin1 promotes remyelination in the neuroinflammatory environment of EAE, presumably by protecting remyelinating oligodendrocytes against inflammatory stress.
source: The data suggest that Sephin1 promotes remyelination in the neuroinflammatory environment of EAE, presumably by protecting remyelinating oligodendrocytes against inflammatory stress.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Myelinating oligodendrocytes with a Ppp1r15a (Gadd34) mutation display increased levels of p-eIF2α in response to IFN-γ.
source: We have previously shown that in response to IFN-γ, myelinating oligodendrocytes with a Ppp1r15a (Gadd34) mutation display increased levels of p-eIF2α, indicating a prolongation of the ISR, and increased oligodendrocyte survival (Lin et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Myelinating oligodendrocytes with a Ppp1r15a (Gadd34) mutation show increased oligodendrocyte survival in response to IFN-γ.
source: We have previously shown that in response to IFN-γ, myelinating oligodendrocytes with a Ppp1r15a (Gadd34) mutation display increased levels of p-eIF2α, indicating a prolongation of the ISR, and increased oligodendrocyte survival (Lin et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Cuprizone-fed mice exhibit apoptotic death of oligodendrocytes and demyelination in the corpus callosum.
source: It has been demonstrated that cuprizone-fed mice exhibit apoptotic death of oligodendrocytes and demyelination in the corpus callosum. Complete remyelination spontaneously occurs a few weeks after the cuprizone challenge is terminated (Matsushima and Morell, 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Complete remyelination spontaneously occurs a few weeks after the cuprizone challenge is terminated.
source: It has been demonstrated that cuprizone-fed mice exhibit apoptotic death of oligodendrocytes and demyelination in the corpus callosum. Complete remyelination spontaneously occurs a few weeks after the cuprizone challenge is terminated (Matsushima and Morell, 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: There was no significant difference in the number of ASPA+ cells between GADD34 wildtype (WT) and GADD34 KO, GFAP-tTA;TRE-IFN-γ double-transgenic mice before cuprizone exposure.
source: We found no significant difference in the number of cells labeled with the mature oligodendrocyte marker ASPA between GADD34 wildtype (WT) and GADD34 KO, GFAP-tTA;TRE-IFN-γ double-transgenic mice before cuprizone exposure (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: After 5 weeks on cuprizone chow, both GADD34 WT and KO double-transgenic mice presented with a significantly reduced number of ASPA+ mature oligodendrocytes in the presence of IFN-γ (IFN-γ+) (WT, p<0.001; KO, p<0.05).
source: After 5 weeks on cuprizone chow, both GADD34 WT and KO double-transgenic mice presented similarly with a significantly reduced number of ASPA+ mature oligodendrocytes in the presence of IFN-γ (IFN-γ+) (WT, p<0.001; KO, p<0.05) (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A,B with statistical analysis.

claim: In the presence of IFN-γ (IFN-γ+), the number of ASPA+ cells dropped in the lesions of WT double-transgenic mice to roughly 500/mm2 (p<0.05).
source: In the presence of IFN-γ (IFN-γ+), this number dropped in the lesions of WT double-transgenic mice to roughly 500/mm2 of ASPA+ cells (p<0.05) (Figure 3A,C), which is consistent with our previous finding that IFN-γ expression in the CNS suppresses the repopulation of oligodendrocytes following cuprizone-induced oligodendrocyte toxicity (Lin et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A,C with statistical analysis.

claim: IFN-γ expression in the CNS suppresses the repopulation of oligodendrocytes following cuprizone-induced oligodendrocyte toxicity.
source: In the presence of IFN-γ (IFN-γ+), this number dropped in the lesions of WT double-transgenic mice to roughly 500/mm2 of ASPA+ cells (p<0.05) (Figure 3A,C), which is consistent with our previous finding that IFN-γ expression in the CNS suppresses the repopulation of oligodendrocytes following cuprizone-induced oligodendrocyte toxicity (Lin et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Compared to GADD34 WT, GFAP-tTA;TRE-IFN-γ mice with the Gadd34 mutation had significantly increased numbers of ASPA+ oligodendrocytes during remyelination in the presence of IFN-γ (IFN-γ+/W8) (p<0.01).
source: Compared to GADD34 WT, GFAP-tTA;TRE-IFN-γ mice with the Gadd34 mutation had significantly increased numbers of ASPA+ oligodendrocytes during remyelination in the presence of IFN-γ (IFN-γ+/W8) (p<0.01) (Figure 3A,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A,C with statistical analysis.

claim: After 5 weeks of cuprizone chow, a significant number of axons exhibited myelin sheath loss in control mice (IFN-γ-), compared to 0 weeks (WT, p<0.0001; KO, p<0.001).
source: After 5 weeks of cuprizone chow, a significant number of axons exhibited myelin sheath loss in control mice (IFN-γ-), compared to 0 weeks (WT, p<0.0001; KO, p<0.001) (Figure 4A,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A,C with statistical analysis.

claim: Both WT and KO double-transgenic mice presented with markedly reduced numbers of myelinated axons in the presence of IFN-γ (IFN-γ+) (WT: 25.2 ± 3.0%, p<0.0001; KO: 24.4 ± 2.7%, p<0.0001).
source: Similarly, both WT and KO double-transgenic mice presented with markedly reduced numbers of myelinated axons in the presence of IFN-γ (IFN-γ+) (WT: 25.2 ± 3.0%, p<0.0001; KO: 24.4 ± 2.7%, p<0.0001).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: No difference in the percentage of myelinated axons was observed between IFN-γ+ and IFN-γ- groups at 5 weeks of cuprizone exposure.
source: Nevertheless, no difference in the percentage of myelinated axons was observed between IFN-γ+ and IFN-γ- groups (Figure 4A,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A,C.

claim: At 3 weeks after cuprizone withdrawal, both IFN-γ-repressed WT and KO mice (IFN-γ-) showed spontaneous remyelination (WT: 42.7 ± 6.2%; KO: 42.6 ± 4.7%).
source: At 3 weeks after cuprizone withdrawal, both IFN-γ-repressed WT and KO mice (IFN-γ-) showed spontaneous remyelination (WT: 42.7 ± 6.2%; KO: 42.6 ± 4.7%) (Figure 4B,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B,D.

claim: Remyelination was significantly suppressed in the corpus callosum of IFN-γ-expressing WT mice (WT: 29.4 ± 2.9%) (p<0.05).
source: Meanwhile, remyelination was significantly suppressed in the corpus callosum of IFN-γ-expressing WT mice (WT: 29.4 ± 2.9%) (p<0.05), but not in that of IFN-γ-expressing KO mice (KO: 49.1 ± 8.8%) (Figure 4B,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B,D with statistical analysis.

claim: Remyelination was not suppressed in the corpus callosum of IFN-γ-expressing KO mice (KO: 49.1 ± 8.8%).
source: Meanwhile, remyelination was significantly suppressed in the corpus callosum of IFN-γ-expressing WT mice (WT: 29.4 ± 2.9%) (p<0.05), but not in that of IFN-γ-expressing KO mice (KO: 49.1 ± 8.8%) (Figure 4B,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B,D.

claim: Prolonging the ISR has no impact in the absence of IFN-γ, but it results in increased repopulation of oligodendrocytes and remyelination following demyelination in the presence of IFN-γ.
source: Together, these data suggest that prolonging the ISR has no impact in the absence of IFN-γ, but it results in increased repopulation of oligodendrocytes and remyelination following demyelination in the presence of IFN-γ.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Sephin1 treatment can prolong the ISR in primary oligodendrocytes exposed to IFN-γ, as shown by prolonged elevated eIF2α phosphorylation levels.
source: We have previously demonstrated that Sephin1 treatment can prolong the ISR in primary oligodendrocytes exposed to IFN-γ, as shown by prolonged elevated eIF2α phosphorylation levels (Chen et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Sephin1 protects mature oligodendrocytes against inflammation in the EAE model.
source: In addition, Sephin1 protects mature oligodendrocytes against inflammation in the EAE model (Chen et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Mice removed from Dox (IFN-γ+) expressed significantly higher levels of IFN-γ in the cerebellum than mice on Dox water (IFN-γ-) at 5 weeks and 8 weeks of cuprizone treatment in all groups.
source: We first examined IFN-γ expression in the double-transgenic mice, which showed that mice removed from Dox (IFN-γ+) expressed significantly higher levels of IFN-γ in the cerebellum than mice on Dox water (IFN-γ-) at 5 weeks and 8 weeks of cuprizone treatment in all groups (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 3 weeks of cuprizone exposure led to a significant decrease of the ASPA+ oligodendrocytes in both IFN-γ- (p<0.01) and IFN-γ+ (p<0.01) groups.
source: Next, we investigated the number of mature oligodendrocytes in the corpus callosum by immunofluorescent staining of ASPA. 3 weeks of cuprizone exposure led to a significant decrease of the ASPA+ oligodendrocytes in both IFN-γ- (p<0.01) and IFN-γ+ (p<0.01) groups (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A,B with statistical analysis.

claim: Oligodendrocytes start regenerating after significant loss at 3 weeks, even in the presence of cuprizone.
source: It has been shown that oligodendrocytes start regenerating after significant loss at 3 weeks, even in the presence of cuprizone (Armstrong et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: A further reduction in the number of oligodendrocytes was observed in the presence of IFN-γ at 5 weeks of cuprizone exposure (p<0.01).
source: We observed a further reduction in the number of oligodendrocytes in the presence of IFN-γ (p<0.01), although we found no difference between vehicle and Sephin1 treatment (veh: 315 ± 44/mm2; Seph 394 ± 67/mm2) (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A,B with statistical analysis.

claim: No difference was found between vehicle and Sephin1 treatment in oligodendrocyte numbers at 5 weeks of cuprizone exposure (veh: 315 ± 44/mm2; Seph 394 ± 67/mm2).
source: We observed a further reduction in the number of oligodendrocytes in the presence of IFN-γ (p<0.01), although we found no difference between vehicle and Sephin1 treatment (veh: 315 ± 44/mm2; Seph 394 ± 67/mm2) (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: At 3 weeks after cuprizone withdrawal, the density of oligodendrocytes returned to the initial levels seen at week 0 (W0) in both vehicle- and Sephin1-treated mice in the absence of IFN-γ.
source: At 3 weeks after cuprizone withdrawal, the density of oligodendrocytes returned to the initial levels seen at week 0 (W0) in both vehicle- and Sephin1-treated mice in the absence of IFN-γ.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: Activation of IFN-γ expression by removing Dox (IFN-γ+) suppressed the repopulation of ASPA+ oligodendrocytes in the vehicle treated mice.
source: Activation of IFN-γ expression by removing Dox (IFN-γ+) suppressed the repopulation of ASPA+ oligodendrocytes in the vehicle treated mice, but Sephin1 treatment significantly increased the survival of these cells (veh: 531 ± 32/mm2, Seph: 672 ± 52/mm2, p<0.05, η2 = 0.74) (Figure 5A,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A,C.

claim: Sephin1 treatment significantly increased the survival of ASPA+ oligodendrocytes in the presence of IFN-γ during remyelination (veh: 531 ± 32/mm2, Seph: 672 ± 52/mm2, p<0.05, η2 = 0.74).
source: Activation of IFN-γ expression by removing Dox (IFN-γ+) suppressed the repopulation of ASPA+ oligodendrocytes in the vehicle treated mice, but Sephin1 treatment significantly increased the survival of these cells (veh: 531 ± 32/mm2, Seph: 672 ± 52/mm2, p<0.05, η2 = 0.74) (Figure 5A,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A,C with statistical analysis.

claim: An approximate 50% reduction in the percentage of myelinated axons was observed after 5 weeks of cuprizone exposure in both IFN-γ- and IFN-γ+ double-transgenic mice (p<0.0001).
source: In addition, we observed an approximate 50% reduction in the percentage of myelinated axons after 5 weeks of cuprizone exposure in both IFN-γ- and IFN-γ+ double-transgenic mice (p<0.0001) (Figure 6A,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A,C with statistical analysis.

claim: During remyelination, CNS delivery of IFN-γ resulted in diminished numbers of remyelinated axons (p<0.05).
source: Similar to the changes in oligodendrocyte numbers, our data demonstrated that during remyelination, CNS delivery of IFN-γ resulted in diminished numbers of remyelinated axons (p<0.05), while mice treated with Sephin1 exhibited a significantly higher percentage of remyelinated axons (veh: 30.3 ± 3.3%, Seph: 43.2 ± 4.6%, p<0.01, η2 = 0.72) (Figure 6B,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B,D with statistical analysis.

claim: Mice treated with Sephin1 exhibited a significantly higher percentage of remyelinated axons during remyelination in the presence of IFN-γ (veh: 30.3 ± 3.3%, Seph: 43.2 ± 4.6%, p<0.01, η2 = 0.72).
source: Similar to the changes in oligodendrocyte numbers, our data demonstrated that during remyelination, CNS delivery of IFN-γ resulted in diminished numbers of remyelinated axons (p<0.05), while mice treated with Sephin1 exhibited a significantly higher percentage of remyelinated axons (veh: 30.3 ± 3.3%, Seph: 43.2 ± 4.6%, p<0.01, η2 = 0.72) (Figure 6B,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B,D with statistical analysis.

claim: Pharmacological enhancement of the ISR with Sephin1 has no impact in the absence of IFN-γ, but it can provide protection to remyelinating oligodendrocytes and promote remyelination in the presence of IFN-γ.
source: These data indicate that although the pharmacological enhancement of the ISR with Sephin1 has no impact in the absence of IFN-γ, it can provide protection to remyelinating oligodendrocytes and promote remyelination in the presence of IFN-γ.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Recruitment of OPCs is required for spontaneous remyelination.
source: Recruitment of OPCs is required for spontaneous remyelination, during which OPCs proliferate and migrate to the demyelinated area to mature into functional oligodendrocytes (Huang and Franklin, 2011; Franklin and Ffrench-Constant, 2008a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: During remyelination, OPCs proliferate and migrate to the demyelinated area to mature into functional oligodendrocytes.
source: Recruitment of OPCs is required for spontaneous remyelination, during which OPCs proliferate and migrate to the demyelinated area to mature into functional oligodendrocytes (Huang and Franklin, 2011; Franklin and Ffrench-Constant, 2008a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: GADD34 deficiency did not affect the appearance of PDGFRα+ OPCs near the demyelinated lesions (W5) and remyelinated areas (W8) in the corpus callosum of double-transgenic mice.
source: Using the OPC marker PDGFRα and the proliferation marker Ki67, we noted the appearance of PDGFRα+ OPCs and proliferating OPCs (PDGFRα+/Ki67+) near the demyelinated lesions (W5) and remyelinated areas (W8) in the corpus callosum of double-transgenic mice, which was not affected by GADD34 deficiency (Figure 7A–C) or Sephin1 treatment (Figure 7D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A-C.

claim: Sephin1 treatment did not affect the appearance of PDGFRα+ OPCs near the demyelinated lesions (W5) and remyelinated areas (W8) in the corpus callosum of double-transgenic mice.

claim: At week 5 of cuprizone exposure, the induction of IFN-γ by Dox removal (IFN-γ+) diminished the number of proliferating OPCs (PDGFRα+/Ki67+) in vehicle-treated mice (p<0.05).
source: Interestingly, at week 5 of cuprizone exposure, the induction of IFN-γ by Dox removal (IFN-γ+) diminished the number of proliferating OPCs (PDGFRα+/Ki67+) in vehicle-treated mice (p<0.05), but no difference between vehicle and Sephin1 was found in the number of OPCs in the presence of IFN-γ (Figure 7D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D,E with statistical analysis.

claim: No difference between vehicle and Sephin1 was found in the number of OPCs in the presence of IFN-γ at week 5 of cuprizone exposure.
source: Interestingly, at week 5 of cuprizone exposure, the induction of IFN-γ by Dox removal (IFN-γ+) diminished the number of proliferating OPCs (PDGFRα+/Ki67+) in vehicle-treated mice (p<0.05), but no difference between vehicle and Sephin1 was found in the number of OPCs in the presence of IFN-γ (Figure 7D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D,E.

claim: Recruitment of microglia is required for myelin clearance and efficient initiation of remyelination.
source: Studies have indicated that recruitment of microglia is required for myelin clearance and efficient initiation of remyelination (Neumann et al., 2009; Voss et al., 2012; Gudi et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: A significantly stronger microgliosis was observed in the corpus callosum of double-transgenic mice after 5 weeks of cuprizone chow (W5) and activated microglia persisted after 3 weeks of remyelination (W8).
source: A significantly stronger microgliosis was observed in the corpus callosum of double-transgenic mice after 5 weeks of cuprizone chow (W5) and activated microglia persisted after 3 weeks of remyelination (W8) (Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: In the group of GADD34 KO, the number of IBA1+ cells at W8 was significantly increased in the presence of IFN-γ than those in the absence of IFN-γ.
source: Interestingly, in the group of GADD34 KO and of Sephin1 treatment, the number of IBA1+ cells at W8 was significantly increased in the presence of IFN-γ than those in the absence of IFN-γ (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,C and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A,C), but we did not detect a statistical change in the density of IBA1+ cells between WT mice and KO or between vehicle and Sephin1 treatment (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,C and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,C.

claim: In the group of Sephin1 treatment, the number of IBA1+ cells at W8 was significantly increased in the presence of IFN-γ than those in the absence of IFN-γ.
source: Interestingly, in the group of GADD34 KO and of Sephin1 treatment, the number of IBA1+ cells at W8 was significantly increased in the presence of IFN-γ than those in the absence of IFN-γ (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,C and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A,C), but we did not detect a statistical change in the density of IBA1+ cells between WT mice and KO or between vehicle and Sephin1 treatment (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,C and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A,C.

claim: No statistical change in the density of IBA1+ cells was detected between WT mice and KO.
source: Interestingly, in the group of GADD34 KO and of Sephin1 treatment, the number of IBA1+ cells at W8 was significantly increased in the presence of IFN-γ than those in the absence of IFN-γ (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,C and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A,C), but we did not detect a statistical change in the density of IBA1+ cells between WT mice and KO or between vehicle and Sephin1 treatment (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,C and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,C.

claim: No statistical change in the density of IBA1+ cells was detected between vehicle and Sephin1 treatment.

evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A,C.

claim: BZA is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) that is currently FDA-approved to be used in combination with conjugated estrogen in menopausal women.
source: BZA is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) that is currently FDA-approved to be used in combination with conjugated estrogen in menopausal women (McKeand et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: BZA significantly enhances OPC differentiation and accelerates remyelination in the lysolecithin non-inflammatory demyelination model.
source: Recently, Rankin et al. showed that BZA significantly enhances OPC differentiation and accelerates remyelination in the lysolecithin non-inflammatory demyelination model (Rankin et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Sephin1, BZA, and combined Sephin1/BZA treatment significantly increased ASPA+ oligodendrocyte numbers in the corpus callosum during remyelination in the presence of IFN-γ (W8/ IFN-γ+) (Sephin1: p<0.05, η2 = 0.78; BZA: p<0.01, η2 = 0.67; Sephin1/BZA: p<0.05, η2 = 0.77).
source: At 3 weeks after cuprizone withdrawal, we found that Sephin1, BZA, and combined Sephin1/BZA treatment significantly increased ASPA+ oligodendrocyte numbers in the corpus callosum during remyelination in the presence of IFN-γ (W8/ IFN-γ+) (Sephin1: p<0.05, η2 = 0.78; BZA: p<0.01, η2 = 0.67; Sephin1/BZA: p<0.05, η2 = 0.77) (Figure 8A,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A,C with statistical analysis.

claim: Compared with vehicle controls, a significant increase in the percentage of myelinated axons was noted in the groups treated with Sephin1, BZA, and combined Sephin1/BZA treatment (Sephin1: p<0.05, η2 = 0.81; BZA: p<0.05, η2 = 0.77; Sephin1/BZA: p<0.01, η2 = 0.80).
source: Accordingly, compared with vehicle controls, a significant increase in the percentage of myelinated axons was noted in the groups treated with Sephin1, BZA, and combined Sephin1/BZA treatment (Sephin1: p<0.05, η2 = 0.81; BZA: p<0.05, η2 = 0.77; Sephin1/BZA: p<0.01, η2 = 0.80) (Figure 8B,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B,D with statistical analysis.

claim: No difference between treatment groups was observed either for oligodendrocyte survival or number of remyelinated axons.
source: Nonetheless, no difference between treatment groups was observed either for oligodendrocyte survival or number of remyelinated axons, although the number of remyelinated axons in treatment groups reached pre-lesion levels (Figure 8B,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B,D.

claim: The number of remyelinated axons in treatment groups reached pre-lesion levels.
source: Nonetheless, no difference between treatment groups was observed either for oligodendrocyte survival or number of remyelinated axons, although the number of remyelinated axons in treatment groups reached pre-lesion levels (Figure 8B,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B,D.

claim: The vehicle-treated mice (W8/IFN-γ+) demonstrated significantly thinner myelin than those at W0 (IFN-γ-).
source: In addition to measuring the percentage of myelinated axons, we also examined myelin thickness using EM analysis of g-ratios after remyelination and using W0 as the pre-lesion reference point. The vehicle-treated mice (W8/IFN-γ+) demonstrated significantly thinner myelin than those at W0 (IFN-γ-).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from EM analysis.

claim: Corpora callosa axons in mice receiving the combination treatment of Sephin1 and BZA (g-ratio: 0.778 ± 0.006) reached myelin thickness levels comparable with pre-lesion W0 axons.
source: In contrast, corpora callosa axons in mice receiving the combination treatment of Sephin1 and BZA (g-ratio: 0.778 ± 0.006) reached myelin thickness levels comparable with pre-lesion W0 axons (Figure 8B,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B,E.

claim: The g-ratios of myelinated axons were significantly lower in the combination treatment group than the vehicle-treated group (p<0.01, η2 = 0.77).
source: The g-ratios of myelinated axons were significantly lower in the combination treatment group than the vehicle-treated group (p<0.01, η2 = 0.77) or either of the single treatment group (p<0.05, η2 = 0.72 vs Sephin1, p<0.05, η2 = 0.72 vs BZA).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: The g-ratios of myelinated axons were significantly lower in the combination treatment group than either of the single treatment groups (p<0.05, η2 = 0.72 vs Sephin1, p<0.05, η2 = 0.72 vs BZA).
source: The g-ratios of myelinated axons were significantly lower in the combination treatment group than the vehicle-treated group (p<0.01, η2 = 0.77) or either of the single treatment group (p<0.05, η2 = 0.72 vs Sephin1, p<0.05, η2 = 0.72 vs BZA).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: Endogenous remyelination plays a crucial role in preserving axons and restoring neuronal function, but is frequently insufficient in MS.
source: Endogenous remyelination plays a crucial role in preserving axons and restoring neuronal function, but is frequently insufficient in MS.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the MS field.

claim: The adverse extracellular environment of MS lesions is thought to contribute to remyelination failure.
source: The adverse extracellular environment of MS lesions is thought to contribute to remyelination failure (Chew et al., 2005; Frischer et al., 2015; Kuhlmann et al., 2008; Franklin and Ffrench-Constant, 2008a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: A recent study indicated that the inflammation in MS lesions is a major contributor to impaired remyelination.
source: A recent study, which investigated the differentiation of induced pluripotent stem-cell-derived oligodendrocytes from MS patients, indicated that the inflammation in MS lesions is a major contributor to impaired remyelination, and many remyelinating agents failed to restore impaired differentiation caused by inflammation (Starost et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Many remyelinating agents failed to restore impaired differentiation caused by inflammation.
source: A recent study, which investigated the differentiation of induced pluripotent stem-cell-derived oligodendrocytes from MS patients, indicated that the inflammation in MS lesions is a major contributor to impaired remyelination, and many remyelinating agents failed to restore impaired differentiation caused by inflammation (Starost et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Prolonging the ISR provides protection to mature oligodendrocytes from inflammatory attack.
source: In our previous studies, we demonstrated that prolonging the ISR provides protection to mature oligodendrocytes, which maintain the myelin sheath, from inflammatory attack (Way and Popko, 2016; Way et al., 2015; Lin et al., 2008; Chen et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work by the authors.

claim: A prolonged ISR response protects mature oligodendrocytes during the peak of disease in EAE in a manner not related to direct immunomodulation.
source: We have previously shown that a prolonged ISR response protects mature oligodendrocytes during the peak of disease in EAE in a manner not related to direct immunomodulation (Chen et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Sephin1 treatment, when initiated at the peak of disease, facilitated the clinical recovery of the EAE animals, which correlated with enhanced remyelination.
source: Here, we demonstrated that Sephin1 treatment, when initiated at the peak of disease, facilitated the clinical recovery of the EAE animals, which correlated with enhanced remyelination.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1.

claim: The T cell cytokine IFN-γ is a critical inflammatory mediator of MS/EAE pathogenesis.
source: The T cell cytokine IFN-γ is a critical inflammatory mediator of MS/EAE pathogenesis (Lees and Cross, 2007; Ottum et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: IFN-γ could induce immune transitions of OPCs and oligodendrocytes to an inflammatory state with major histocompatibility complex (MHC)-I and MHC-II presentation.
source: In addition, it has been suggested that IFN-γ could induce immune transitions of OPCs and oligodendrocytes to an inflammatory state with major histocompatibility complex (MHC)-I and MHC-II presentation (Kirby and Castelo-Branco, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Cuprizone-induced demyelination/remyelination occurs in the absence of an adaptive immune response.
source: IFN-γ delivery is required because cuprizone-induced demyelination/remyelination occurs in the absence of an adaptive immune response and thus does not reflect the inflammatory environment in the MS lesions.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the cuprizone model.

claim: The level of IFN-γ present in the CNS of GFAP-tTA;TRE-IFN-γ double transgenic mice is approximately equivalent to that of EAE mice.
source: Importantly, the level of IFN-γ present in the CNS of GFAP-tTA;TRE-IFN-γ double transgenic mice is approximately equivalent to that of EAE mice (data not shown), which suggests that Dox-controlled IFN-γ release is within the range observed in inflammatory demyelination.
evidence: This claim is based on unpublished data mentioned in the manuscript.

claim: Ectopic expression of IFN-γ in the CNS results in a reduction in the number of myelinating oligodendrocytes and hypomyelination during development.
source: Our previous studies with GFAP-tTA;TRE-IFN-γ double-transgenic mice demonstrated that ectopic expression of IFN-γ in the CNS results in a reduction in the number of myelinating oligodendrocytes and hypomyelination during development, and results in diminished remyelination following cuprizone-induced oligodendrocyte toxicity (Lin et al., 2008; Lin et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Ectopic expression of IFN-γ in the CNS results in diminished remyelination following cuprizone-induced oligodendrocyte toxicity.
source: Our previous studies with GFAP-tTA;TRE-IFN-γ double-transgenic mice demonstrated that ectopic expression of IFN-γ in the CNS results in a reduction in the number of myelinating oligodendrocytes and hypomyelination during development, and results in diminished remyelination following cuprizone-induced oligodendrocyte toxicity (Lin et al., 2008; Lin et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: CNS expression of IFN-γ suppresses the repopulation of oligodendrocytes and results in diminished numbers of remyelinated axons following cuprizone-induced demyelination.
source: In our current study we found that CNS expression of IFN-γ suppresses the repopulation of oligodendrocytes and results in diminished numbers of remyelinated axons following cuprizone-induced demyelination.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the current study.

claim: It takes about 2–3 weeks for IFN-γ levels to become elevated in the CNS following the removal of Dox from the animal's diet.
source: In the GFAP-tTA;TRE-IFN-γ model, it takes about 2–3 weeks for IFN-γ levels to become elevated in the CNS following the removal of Dox from the animal's diet (Figure 2—figure supplement 1; Lin et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and a citation.

claim: The majority of mature oligodendrocytes had already been lost (W3) by the time IFN-γ levels became elevated.
source: Since Dox removal occurred at the time of the initiation of cuprizone exposure, the majority of mature oligodendrocytes had already been lost (W3) by the time IFN-γ levels became elevated.
evidence: This is an inference based on the timing of the experimental protocol.

claim: In this model, mainly newly generated remyelinating oligodendrocytes are exposed to IFN-γ.
source: Therefore, in this model, mainly newly generated remyelinating oligodendrocytes are exposed to IFN-γ.
evidence: This is an inference based on the timing of IFN-γ expression and oligodendrocyte loss.

claim: The effect of IFN-γ on the remyelination process in the cuprizone model is associated with an activated ISR response in remyelinating oligodendrocytes.
source: Using the same mouse model, our group previously showed that the effect of IFN-γ on the remyelination process in the cuprizone model is associated with an activated ISR response in remyelinating oligodendrocytes (Lin et al., 2005; Lin et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work by the authors.

claim: GADD34 deficiency or Sephin1 treatment significantly increased the number of remyelinating oligodendrocytes and myelinated axons in the presence of IFN-γ.
source: Indeed, GADD34 deficiency or Sephin1 treatment, both of which prolong the ISR, significantly increased the number of remyelinating oligodendrocytes and myelinated axons in the presence of IFN-γ.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the current study.

claim: The enhancement of the ISR had no effect on remyelination in the absence of IFN-γ.
source: Nevertheless, the enhancement of the ISR had no effect on remyelination in the absence of IFN-γ.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the current study.

claim: Guanabenz, a drug closely related to Sephin1, did not improve remyelination in the non-inflammatory cuprizone model of demyelination.
source: This is consistent with a recent study that showed that guanabenz, a drug closely related to Sephin1 (Das et al., 2015), did not improve remyelination in the non-inflammatory cuprizone model of demyelination (Thompson and Tsirka, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The increased numbers of remyelinating oligodendrocytes that result from an enhanced ISR might originate from increased OPC survival in the lesion or from more efficient OPC differentiation to mature oligodendrocytes.
source: The increased numbers of remyelinating oligodendrocytes that result from an enhanced ISR might originate from increased OPC survival in the lesion or from more efficient OPC differentiation to mature oligodendrocytes.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism underlying the observed effects.

claim: IFN-γ predisposed OPCs to apoptosis.
source: We observed that proliferating OPC numbers at the peak of cuprizone-induced demyelination were diminished by the presence of IFN-γ, which is consistent with previous findings that showed that IFN-γ predisposed OPCs to apoptosis (Chew et al., 2005; Kirby et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Prolonging the ISR by the Gadd34 mutation or by Sephin1 treatment did not alter the number of proliferating OPCs in the presence of inflammation.
source: Nevertheless, prolonging the ISR by the Gadd34 mutation or by Sephin1 treatment did not alter the number of proliferating OPCs in the presence of inflammation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the current study.

claim: The benefits of ISR enhancement on remyelination in the presence of inflammation are primarily due to the protection of actively myelinating oligodendrocytes.
source: Therefore, it is likely that the benefits of ISR enhancement on remyelination in the presence of inflammation are primarily due to the protection of actively myelinating oligodendrocytes, similar to what we have observed during developmental myelination (Chew et al., 2005; Lin et al., 2005).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and previous findings.

claim: BZA can promote remyelination in the presence of the inflammatory cytokine IFN-γ.
source: We show here that BZA can promote remyelination in the presence of the inflammatory cytokine IFN-γ, which provides valuable preclinical support to the current MS clinical trial of BZA as a remyelination-enhancing agent (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04002934).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the current study.

claim: The combination treatment of BZA and Sephin1 resulted in more axons with thicker myelin, indicating a more substantial recovery.
source: Encouragingly, we found that the combination treatment of BZA and Sephin1 resulted in more axons with thicker myelin, indicating a more substantial recovery.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the current study.

claim: The myelin sheaths of remyelinated axons are uniformly thin regardless of axon diameter.
source: The myelin sheaths of remyelinated axons are uniformly thin regardless of axon diameter, but the underlying mechanism that controls the thickness of remyelinated axons is unknown (Fancy et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: The underlying mechanism that controls the thickness of remyelinated axons is unknown.
source: The myelin sheaths of remyelinated axons are uniformly thin regardless of axon diameter, but the underlying mechanism that controls the thickness of remyelinated axons is unknown (Fancy et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: The transgenic overexpression of neuregulin (Nrg) or the conditional knockout of Petn increases myelin sheath thickness in developmental myelination.
source: Although previous studies have shown that the transgenic overexpression of neuregulin (Nrg) or the conditional knockout of Petn increases myelin sheath thickness in developmental myelination, the remyelinated myelin sheaths remain thin in these models (Brinkmann et al., 2008; Harrington et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The remyelinated myelin sheaths remain thin in transgenic models with overexpression of Nrg or conditional knockout of Petn.
source: Although previous studies have shown that the transgenic overexpression of neuregulin (Nrg) or the conditional knockout of Petn increases myelin sheath thickness in developmental myelination, the remyelinated myelin sheaths remain thin in these models (Brinkmann et al., 2008; Harrington et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Increased myelin thickness after the combination treatment of BZA and Sephin1 suggests that remyelination can be more efficiently induced by using therapies promoting OPC differentiation in combination with therapies that protect the remyelinating oligodendrocytes against inflammatory environment.
source: Increased myelin thickness after the combination treatment of BZA and Sephin1 in our inflammatory de/remyelination model suggests that remyelination can be more efficiently induced by using therapies promoting OPC differentiation in combination with therapies that protect the remyelinating oligodendrocytes against inflammatory environment.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from the combination treatment.

claim: Effective MS therapies need to both suppress the aggressive CNS inflammation and promote restoring neuronal functions, including remyelination.
source: Effective MS therapies need to both suppress the aggressive CNS inflammation and promote restoring neuronal functions, including remyelination (Rodgers et al., 2013; Titus et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The ISR modulator Sephin1 protects remyelinating oligodendrocytes in the presence of an inflammatory environment, leading to remarkably improved remyelination.
source: Our current study demonstrates that the ISR modulator Sephin1 protects remyelinating oligodendrocytes in the presence of an inflammatory environment, leading to remarkably improved remyelination.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the current study.

claim: Sephin1 protects mature oligodendrocytes, myelin and axons, in addition to indirectly dampening the CNS inflammation that drives EAE.
source: In our previous EAE study, we showed that Sephin1 protects mature oligodendrocytes, myelin and axons, in addition to indirectly dampening the CNS inflammation that drives EAE (Chen et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Combining Sephin1 with the anti-inflammatory MS drug IFN-β resulted in an additive effect in alleviating EAE.
source: We also showed that combining Sephin1 with the anti-inflammatory MS drug IFN-β resulted in an additive effect in alleviating EAE.
evidence: This claim is supported by previous work mentioned in the manuscript.

claim: Sephin1 or similar ISR enhancing strategies will likely provide significant therapeutic benefit to MS patients when combined with current immunosuppressive treatment.
source: Combining current and previous findings, we believe that Sephin1 or similar ISR enhancing strategies will likely provide significant therapeutic benefit to MS patients when combined with current immunosuppressive treatment.
evidence: This is speculation based on the combined findings from current and previous studies.
